translations.text: The book of the birth of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham fathered Isaac; Isaac fathered Jacob; Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers;
and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar; and Perez fathered Hezron; Hezron fathered Ram;
Ram fathered Amminadab; Amminadab fathered Nahshon; Nahshon fathered Salmon;
Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab; Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth; Obed fathered Jesse;
Jesse begot David the king; David the king begot Solomon by the wife of Uriah;
Solomon fathered Rehoboam; Rehoboam fathered Abijah; Abijah fathered Asaph;
Asaph begot Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat begot Joram; Joram begot Uzziah;
Uzziah fathered Jotham; Jotham fathered Ahaz; Ahaz fathered Hezekiah;
Hezekiah begot Manasseh; Manasseh begot Amon; Amon begot Josiah;
Josiah begot Jehoiakim; Jehoiakim begot Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the captivity by the Babylonians.
After the Babylonian captivity, Jeconiah begot Shealtiel; Shealtiel begot Zerubbabel;
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud; Abiud fathered Eliakim; Eliakim fathered Azor;
Azor fathered Zadok; Zadok fathered Achim; Achim fathered Eliud;
Eliud fathered Eleazar; Eleazar fathered Matthan; Matthan fathered Jacob;
Jacob begot Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

All the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the captivity by the Babylonians, fourteen generations; and from the Babylonian captivity to Christ, fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was thus: his mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, and before they came together she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
But Joseph her husband was righteous and did not wish to expose her; he resolved to send her away secretly.

And as he was only considering this, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a vision and said to him: "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary your wife, for what will be born of her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will bear a son, and they will call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
All this came to pass so that the word of the Lord spoken through the mouth of the prophet might be fulfilled:
Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel, which in translation is: God with us.
Joseph awoke from his sleep and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took his wife to himself.
And he did not know her until she bore that son of hers, the firstborn, and they called his name Jesus.
Now when Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod, behold, Magi came from the east to Jerusalem and said:
Where is the newborn King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him.
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
And he gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people and inquired of them: Where is the Christ to be born?
And they said to him: In Bethlehem of Judea. For thus it is written by the prophet:
And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah, for from you will come forth a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.
Then Herod secretly summoned the Magi and ascertained from them the time of the star's appearing.
And he sent them to Bethlehem and said to them: Go and inquire carefully about the child, and when you find him, tell me, so that I too may go and worship him.
And when they had heard this from the king, they departed. And behold, the star that they had seen in the east went before them, until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy.
And when they entered the house and saw the child with Mary his mother, they fell down and worshiped him; and they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, incense, and myrrh.
And they received a command in a vision from an angel not to return to Herod, but to depart by another road to their own country.

And when they had gone away, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a vision to Joseph and said to him: Arise, take the child and his mother, flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod intends to seek out the child and destroy him.
And he arose and took the child and his mother by night, and departed to Egypt, and stayed there until the death of Herod,
so that the word of the Lord spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: Out of Egypt I called my son.

Then Herod, when he saw that he had been mocked by the magi, became furious, and he sent and slaughtered all the children who were in Bethlehem and in all its territory, from two years old and under, according to the time that he had ascertained from the magi.
Then what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
A voice was heard in Ramah, of lamentation and weeping and great crying out; Rachel was weeping for her children and would not accept consolation, because they are no more.
But when Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
and said to him: "Rise, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child's life are dead."
And he arose and took the child and his mother and came to the land of Israel.

And when he heard that Archelaus was reigning in Judea in place of Herod his father, he was afraid to go there; but he received a command from an angel in a vision and went away to the land of Galilee.
And he came and settled in the city called Nazareth, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: He shall be called a Nazarene.
In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea
and he was saying: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
For this is the one of whom it was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, who said: The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord and make his places straight.
Now John himself wore clothing made of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist; and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then all the people of Jerusalem and of Judea and of the country around the Jordan went out to him.
And they were baptized by him in the river Jordan and confessed their sins.
And when he saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized by him, he said to them: "Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come?"
So now bear fruit worthy of repentance,
And do not suppose and say among yourselves: We have Abraham as our father. But this I tell you: God is able to raise up from these stones children for Abraham.
For even now, look, the axe lies at the roots of the trees. Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
Now I baptize you with water for repentance. But he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not able to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hands; he will cleanse his threshing floor and gather the wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
But John tried to prevent him, saying to him: "I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?"
But Jesus answered and said to him: Allow it now, for thus it is right for us to fulfil all righteousness. Then John permitted him.
And Jesus was baptized. And when he was coming up from the water, behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove; it came and rested upon him.
And there was a voice from heaven, and it said: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
And he fasted forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.
And the tempter approached him and said: If you are the Son of God, speak, so that these stones may become bread.
But Jesus answered and said: It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes out of the mouth of God.
Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the pinnacle of the temple

and said to him: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here to the ground, for it is written: He has commanded his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up on their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
Jesus said to him: Again it is written thus: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory
And he said to him: "All these I will give you, if you fall down and worship me."
Then Jesus said to him: Get away from me, back, devil, for it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.
Then the devil left him, and angels came and served him.
When Jesus heard that John had been handed over to prison, he withdrew and went away to Galilee.
And he left Nazareth and came and settled in Capernaum, beside the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali,
so that the word spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
"Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles:
The people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and on those who sat in darkness and the shadows of death, a light appeared.
From then on Jesus began to preach and to say: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
And as Jesus was walking by the shore of the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And he said to them: "Come and follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
And they immediately left their net and followed him.
And he went on from there and saw two brothers, James son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, as they were mending their nets, and he called them.
And they immediately left the boat and their father and followed him.
And Jesus went around all Galilee and taught in their synagogue and preached the kingdom and healed every sickness among the people.

And the report of him spread through all the land of Syria. And they brought to him all who were grievously sick with various kinds of diseases, those seized by torments, the demon-possessed, the moonstruck, and the paralyzed, and he healed them.
And a great crowd followed him from Galilee and the Ten Cities and Jerusalem and Judea and from beyond the Jordan, and he healed them.
And when Jesus saw the crowd, he went up on the mountain and sat down there. And his disciples came to him.
And he opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
"Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn in heart, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall receive mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.
Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are you when they reproach you and persecute you and falsely say every evil word against you for my sake.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you.
You are the salt of the earth. If the salt loses its savor, with what shall it be salted? From then on it is no longer of any use, except to be thrown out and trampled by people.
You are the lights of the world. A city built on a mountain cannot be hidden.
Nor do people light a lamp and put it under a bushel, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
In the same way let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have not come to abolish, but to fulfil.
Amen, I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, not a single iota, not one stroke, shall pass away from the law and the prophets until everything comes to pass.

If anyone breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches people so, he shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does them and teaches them, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
But I say to you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill; and whoever kills is liable to death.

But I say to you that whoever becomes angry with his brother without cause is liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother 'raca,' which means loathsome, is liable to be put out of the assembly; and whoever says to his brother 'fool' is liable to the Gehenna of fire.
If you are offering your offering on the altar and there you remember that your brother has some grievance against you,
Leave that offering before the altar and go first and be reconciled with your brother, and then come and offer your offering.

Be on good terms with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the road, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the magistrate, and the magistrate hand you over to the servants, and they throw you into prison.
Amen I say to you: you will not come out from there until you have paid a fraction of a dang [a small coin].
You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not commit adultery.
But I say to you: everyone who looks at a woman and desires her has at once committed adultery with her in his heart.

If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members should perish than that your whole body should fall into the Gehenna of fire.

And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it away from you, for it is better for you that one of your members should perish and not that your whole body should fall into Gehenna.
It has been said that whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.
But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of fornication, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman also commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not swear falsely, but you shall render to the Lord what you have sworn.
But I say to you not to swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Do not swear by your head either, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your yes be yes and your no be no. Anything more than these comes from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said: An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.
But I say to you not to resist the evil person; rather, whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other as well.
And whoever wishes to take you to court and take your tunic, let him have your garment as well.
And whoever forces you into service for one mile, go with him two as well.
Give to whoever asks of you; and do not turn away from whoever wishes to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: love your enemies, and bless those who curse you, and do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who oppress you and persecute you,
so that you may be sons of your Father in heaven, for his sun spreads over the evil and the good, and he sends rain on the righteous and on sinners.
If you love only those who love you, what reward do you have? For tax collectors and sinners also do the same.
And if you greet only your friends, what more are you doing? Or do not tax collectors and sinners also do the same?
Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Take care with your almsgiving, that you do not do it before people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.

But when you do your almsgiving, do not proclaim it before you, as the hypocrites do in their synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by people. Amen I say to you: they have received their reward.
But you, when you do almsgiving, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your almsgiving may be in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you openly.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, so that they may be seen by people. Amen, I say to you: they have received their reward.
But when you pray, go into your storeroom and shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will reward you openly.
And when you pray, do not say many words, as the Gentiles do, for they think that they will be heard because of their many words.
But do not be like them, for your heavenly Father knows what you need before you ask him.
But you, pray in this way: Our Father who are in heaven, holy be your name,
may your kingdom come, may your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us today our daily bread,
and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil, for yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory, to the ages, forever. Amen.
If you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
If you do not forgive people their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive you your trespasses.
And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Amen, I tell you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
so that you may not appear to people as one who is fasting, but to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees hidden things, will repay you.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moth and devourer destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal.
But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not dig through and steal.
For where your wealth is, there also your heart will be.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
If your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. If the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
It is not possible to serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to the one and despise the other. It is not possible to serve God and mammon.
Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your soul, what you will eat and drink, nor about your flesh, what you will wear. Is not the soul more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky, for they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather treasure, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much better than the birds?
Who among you, by being anxious, is able to add one cubit to his stature?
And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow! They do not toil, nor do they spin.
But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
If God so clothes the grass of the field, which exists today and tomorrow is kindled in the oven, how much more you, O you of little faith?
Do not worry, saying, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?'
For the Gentiles seek all these things, for your Father knows that you need all of these.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
Do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for that day is its own evil.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged,
for with the judgment with which you judge, you will be judged, and with the measure with which you measure out, it will be measured out to you.
Or why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, and do not consider the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, 'Allow me, and I will take the speck out of your eye,' and behold, there is the beam in your own eye!
Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give my holy thing to dogs, nor spread your pearl before swine, lest they trample it with their feet and turn and tear you apart.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
Or who among you is the man whose son asks him for bread: will he give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake?
If you, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him!
Everything that you want people to do to you, do likewise to them, for such is the law and the prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many walk on it.
How narrow is the gate and hard the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will know them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
So every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.
Every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
By their works indeed you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?'
Then I will say to them, 'I do not know you; depart from me, all you workers of lawlessness.'
Everyone who hears these words and does them will be like the prudent man who built his house on rock.
And the rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon the rock.
And everyone who hears these words and does not do them is like the foolish man who built his house on sand.
And the rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell. And its fall was very great.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowd was astonished at his teaching,
For his teaching to them was like that of one who had authority, and not like that of their scribes.
And as he was coming down from the mountain, a great crowd followed him.
And behold, a certain leper came to him, worshipped him and said to him: "Lord, if you will, you are able to cleanse me."
And Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him: "I will it; be cleansed!" And immediately he was cleansed of his leprosy.
And Jesus said to him: "See that you tell no one, but go and show yourself to the priests, and offer your offering, which Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
And as he entered Capernaum, a centurion came to him, entreating him
and saying: "Lord, my servant is lying in my house paralyzed, and he is grievously tormented."
Jesus said to him: "I will come and heal him."
The centurion answered and said to him: "Lord, I am not worthy that you should come in under my roof; but only say it with a word, and my servant will be healed."
for I too am a man under authority, and I have soldiers under me; and I say to one, 'Go!' and he goes; and to another, 'Come!' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, he marveled and said to the crowd who were following him: "Amen I say to you: not even in Israel have I found so great a faith."
"But I say to you that many will come from the east and the west and will recline with Abraham and with Isaac and with Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,"
but the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."

And Jesus said to the centurion: "Go, and as you have believed, let it be done for you." And his servant was healed on that day. And when the centurion came to his house, he found his servant healed at that hour.
And Jesus came to Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law lying ill with a fever.
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; she rose and served him.
And when it became evening, they brought to him many who were possessed by demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word, and he healed all who were grievously sick,
so that what was said by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said: "He bore our infirmities and healed our sicknesses."
When Jesus saw a great crowd around him, he gave orders to cross over to the other side.
And a certain scribe came to him and said: "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
Jesus said to him: "The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have dwelling places, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
And one of his disciples said to him: "Teacher, command me first to go and bury my father."
But Jesus said to him: "Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead."
And as he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And behold, there was a great tempest on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves. But he himself was asleep.
And his disciples came to him and roused the Lord and said to him: "Lord, save us, for we are perishing!"
And he said to them: "Why are you afraid, you of little faith?" Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea. And immediately there was a great calm.
But the men marveled and said: "What sort of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
And when he came to the far side, to the country of the Gergesenes, two demon-possessed men met him, coming out from the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one was able to pass along that road.
And they cried out and said: "What is there between us and you, Jesus, Son of God? For you have come here before the time to torment us."
And far from them there was a herd of swine feeding.
And the demons begged him, saying: "If you cast us out, permit us to go into that herd of swine."
And he said to them: "Go!" And they went out of the men and went off to the herd of swine. And the herd of swine rushed to the steep bank of the sea, and they perished in the waters.
And the herdsmen fled, went into the city, and told everything, including what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
Then the whole city came out to meet Jesus. And when they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
And he got into a boat, crossed over, and came to his own city.
Then they brought to him a paralytic lying on a bed. And Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralytic: "Do not be afraid, child; your sins are forgiven you."
And there some of the scribes said in their hearts: "This man blasphemes."
Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them: "Why do you think evil in your hearts?"
For what is easier, to say: "Your sins are forgiven you," or to say: "Arise and walk"?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — then he said to the paralyzed man: "Rise, take up your bed, and go to your house!"
And at once he rose and went to his house.
When the crowd saw this, they were amazed and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
And Jesus went on from there and saw a man who was sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name, and said to him: "Follow me!" And he arose and followed him.
And it happened that as he was reclining at table in the house, many tax collectors and sinners were reclining at table with Jesus and his disciples.
When those Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples: "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
But when Jesus heard this, he said to them: "Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick."
"But you, go and learn what this means: I desire mercy and not sacrifice. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Then the disciples of John came to him and said: "Why do we and the Pharisees fast much, but your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus said to them: "Can the sons of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? Days will come when that bridegroom is taken up from them, and then they will fast."
"No one puts a patch of unfulled cloth on an old garment, for its fullness pulls away from the garment, and a greater tear is made."
"Nor do they pour new wine into old wineskins, lest the wineskins burst, and the wine be spilled, and the wineskins be ruined. But they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved."
And while he was saying this to them, a certain ruler came to him, bowed down before him and said to him: "My daughter has just now died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
And Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples with him.
And behold, a certain woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years came up behind him and touched the hem of his garment.
For she said in her heart: "If I only touch his garment, I shall be saved."
But Jesus turned, saw her and said to her: "Do not be afraid, daughter; your faith has healed you." And the woman was healed from that hour.
And Jesus came to the house of the ruler and saw there the flute players, and the crowd gathered, and the uproar,
and he said to them: "Go away, for the girl is not dead, but sleeping." But they ridiculed him.
And when he had put the crowd out, he went in and took her by the hand, and raised the girl up.
And this report spread through all that land.
And as Jesus was going on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying: "Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!"
And when Jesus had entered the house, those blind men came to him, and Jesus said to them: "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" They said to him: "Yes, Lord."
Then he touched their eyes and said to them: "According to your faith let it be done to you!"
And immediately their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them and said: "See that no one knows."
But they went out and spread it abroad through all that land.
And just as they were going out, they brought to him a deaf man possessed by a demon.
And when he had cast out that demon, the deaf man spoke soundly. And the people marveled and said: "Never has anything like this appeared in Israel."
But the Pharisees said: "By the prince of demons he casts out demons."
And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.
And when he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, for they were weary and scattered, like sheep that have no shepherd.
Then he said to his disciples: "The harvest is great, but the workers are few."
"Pray to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out workers into his harvest."
And he called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they would cast them out and heal every disease and every infirmity.
Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first Simon, who was called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother,
Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, James the son of Alphaeus and Lebbaeus, who was called Thaddaeus,
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
These twelve Jesus sent out, commanded them and said: "Do not go on the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans,"
but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And as you go, preach and say: 'The kingdom of heaven has come near.'
"Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons; freely you received, freely also give."
"Do not take gold, nor silver, nor brass in your belts,"
"nor a bag for the road, nor two garments, nor sandals, nor a staff, for the laborer is worthy of his wage."
Whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
And as you enter that house, greet it and say: 'Peace to this house!'
"And if that house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you."
"And if no one receives you or listens to your words, when you go out from that house or from that city, shake off the dust of your feet."
"Amen I say to you: it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city."
"Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. So be wise as serpents and innocent as doves."
Beware of people, for they will hand you over to councils, and they will torment you in their synagogues,
And they will bring you before rulers and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
And when they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you will say, for what you are to say will be given to you in that hour.
For it will not be you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and father his child; and children will rise up against their fathers and mothers and will kill them.
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name, but whoever endures, that one will be fully saved.

When they persecute you out of this city, flee to another; and if they persecute you from there too, flee to another place. Amen I say to you: you will not finish the cities of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple is not greater than his teacher, and a servant is not greater than his master.
It is enough for the disciple if he is like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they call the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more his household?
So do not be afraid of them, for nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing is secret that will not be made known.
What is said to you in the dark, say in the light, and what you hear in your ears, proclaim on the rooftops.
And do not be afraid of those who kill the body but have no power to kill the soul; rather, fear more the one who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Or are not two sparrows sold for one assarion? And not even one of them falls to the ground without your Father.
And even the hairs of your head are all counted.
Do not be afraid of them, for you are better than many sparrows.
Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge him before my Father in heaven.
And whoever denies me before people, I too will deny before my Father in heaven.
Do not think that I came to spread peace upon the earth. I did not come to spread peace, but a sword.
For I came to divide a man from his father, and a daughter from her mother, and a daughter-in-law from her mother-in-law.
And a man's enemies will be those of his own household.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever finds his life will lose it; and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
Whoever receives you has received me; and whoever receives me has received the Father who sent me.

Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet's reward. And whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person's reward.
And whoever gives one of these little ones a single cup of cool water to drink in the name of a disciple, amen, I tell you, his reward will not be lost.
And it happened that, when Jesus had finished giving these commands to his twelve disciples, he went on from there to preach and teach in their cities.
Now when John heard in prison of those works of Christ, he sent his disciples
and said to him: "Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
And Jesus answered and said to them: "Go and tell John what you hear and see:
The blind see again, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, and the dead rise, and the poor have good news brought to them,
And blessed is he who does not stumble on account of me."
And as these were going away, Jesus began to speak to the people about John: What did you go out to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out for? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are dressed in soft clothing are in royal houses.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet!
For this is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I will send my angel before you, who will prepare your ways before you.
Amen I say to you: no one born of women has arisen greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
For from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven is taken by force, and those who use force will seize it.
For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John,
and if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah, who is to come.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
Now to whom shall I compare this generation? It is like children who sit in the streets and call out to their companions
And they said to them: We piped for you, and you did not dance; we mourned to you, and you did not beat your breasts.
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say: Behold, a man who is a glutton and a wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners. And wisdom was justified by her children.
Then Jesus began to reproach the cities where most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent:
"Woe to you, Chorazin, and woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works that were done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth on ashes.
But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on that day of judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, do not be exalted to heaven, but you will go down to hell; for if the mighty works that were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this very day.
But I tell you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on that day of judgment than for you.
At that time Jesus spoke and said: "I confess to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned and have revealed them to little children.
Yes, Father, for so it was pleasing in your sight.

All things have been given to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father; nor does anyone know the Father except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him, he will reveal him to that person.
Come to me, all who are weary and who carry a heavy burden, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls,
for my yoke is sweet, and the burden is small.
At that time Jesus was going through the grainfields on the Sabbath day. And his disciples became hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
But when the Pharisees saw this, they said to him: Behold, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.
But he said to them: "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him?
How he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the offerings, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests.
Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are blameless?
But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
If you had known what this means: I desire mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the blameless.
For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath also.
And Jesus went on from there and came into their synagogue.
And there was a man there whose hand was withered. And they questioned him, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath? -- so that they might accuse him.
But Jesus said to them: "What man among you who has one sheep, if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much better is a man than a sheep? Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.
Then Jesus said to that man: Stretch out your hand! -- And he stretched out his hand, and it was restored to life, like the other one.
But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him; but Jesus perceived it, and withdrew from there and went away.
And a great crowd followed him, and he healed them all.
And he ordered them not to make him known,
so that what was spoken by Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which says:
Behold, my servant, in whom I am well pleased, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. And I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.
He will not quarrel, nor cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.
A crushed reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings forth judgment to victory.
And in his name the Gentiles will hope."
Then they brought to him a demon-possessed man, blind and deaf, and he healed him, so that the deaf and blind man saw and spoke.
And the crowd was amazed, and they said: Could this be the Son of David?
But when the Pharisees heard this, they said: "This man casts out demons only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons."
Jesus knew the thoughts of their hearts and said to them: Every kingdom that is divided against itself becomes desolate. And every city or house that is divided against itself becomes desolate.
And if the devil casts out devils, he has been divided [?] against himself; how then is his kingdom firm?
And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will be your judges.
If I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Or how can anyone enter the house of a strong man and carry off his vessels, unless he first binds the strong man, and only then plunders his house?
Whoever is not with me is my enemy, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you: every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven people.
And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this world nor in the next.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit.
Offspring of vipers, how can you speak what is good, since you are wicked? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good man brings out good from his good treasure, and the evil man brings out evil from his evil treasure.
But I say to you: for every idle word that people speak, they will give an account on the day of judgment,
for by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered and said to him: Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.
But he answered and said to them: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.
For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn them, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the South will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
But when the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it wanders through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it.
Then it says: I will return to my house, from which I came out. And it comes and finds it vacant, beautified and adorned.

Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they come and settle there. And the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be also for this wicked generation.
And while he was still speaking to the crowd, behold, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak with him.
Then someone said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside and want to say something to you.
But Jesus answered and said to the one speaking: Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?
And he stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said: Behold my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat down by the seashore.
And a great crowd gathered to him, so that he went into a boat and sat down. And the whole crowd stood on the seashore.
And he spoke many things to them in parables and said: Behold, a sower went out to sow,
and as he sowed, some fell on the road, and the birds of the sky came and ate it.
And another part fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil; and it sprang up at once, and because there was no depth of soil,
the sun rose, and it grew hot, and because it had not put down roots, it withered.
And other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked it.
And some fell on good ground and gave fruit: some a hundredfold, and some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And his disciples came to him and said to him: Why do you speak to them in parables?
And Jesus said to them: To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.
For whoever has, to him it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
For this reason I speak to them in parables, because they see and do not see, and they hear and do not hear, nor do they understand.
And the prophecy of the prophet Isaiah is fulfilled in them: Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.

For the heart of this people has grown thick, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and their eyes they have shut, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I should heal them.
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Amen I say to you: many prophets and righteous people longed in their hearts to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.
So you, hear this parable of the sower.
Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches the seed from his heart: this is the one that was sown along the road.
And the one that was sown on rocky ground is this: the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy in his heart.
But he has no root in his heart, and is only for this passing time. And when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, he immediately stumbles.
And the one that was sown among the thorns is this: the one who hears the word, and the care of this world and the deceit of riches choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And the one that was sown on good ground is this: the one who heard the word and understood it, who brought forth fruit and produced, one a hundred, one sixty, and one thirty.
He set another parable before them and said: The kingdom of God is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
And while the men were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat and went away.
When the blade sprouted and brought forth fruit, then the tares appeared.
The servants came and told the master of the house, and said to him: Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where did the tares spring up?
And he said to them: An enemy has done this. And the servants said to him: Do you want us to go and pick them out?
But he said to them: No, lest in gathering the tares you uproot the wheat along with them.

Let them grow together with one another until the time of the harvest, and at the time of the harvest I will command the reapers: Gather the tares first and bind them in sheaves to be burned, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.
He told them another parable, saying: "The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his own garden."
It is the smallest of all seeds, but when it grows, it is greater than all the herbs, and it becomes a great tree, so that the birds of heaven come and settle in its branches.
Then he spoke another parable to them and said: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until it had leavened all of it.
All this Jesus spoke to the people in parables, and without a parable he said nothing to them,
so that the word spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: I will open my mouth in parables and speak parables from the beginning of the world.
Then Jesus left the people and came to the house. And his disciples approached him and said to him: Tell us the parable of the tares and the field.
And he answered and said to them: The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man;
and the field is this world; and the good seeds are the sons of the kingdom, and the tares are the sons of the evil one.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of this world, and the reapers are the angels."
Just as the tares are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of this world."
For the Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness
and they will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of heaven. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid, and in his joy over it he went and sold everything he had, and bought that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant who was seeking fine pearls.
When he found one pearl of great price, he went and sold everything he had and bought it."
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet which is cast into the sea, which gathers fish of every kind.
And when it is full, they bring it out and pour it out on the seashore, and they gather the good into a vessel, but the worthless they throw away.
So it will be at the end of this world: for the angels will come forth and separate the wicked from among the righteous
and cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Jesus said to his disciples: "Have you understood all this?" And they said to him: "Yes, Lord."
And he said to them: "Therefore every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a man, the master of a house, who brings out of his treasury things old and new."
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there,
And he came to his homeland and taught them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished and said: "Where does this man get this wisdom and power?
Is this not the son of the carpenter? Is his mother not called Mary? And his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And are his sisters not all among us? Where does this man get all this?"
And they took offence at him. But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honour, except in his own country and in his own house."
And he did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
At that time Herod, the ruler of the four principalities, heard the report about Jesus,
and he said to his servants: "This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead, and that is why these powers are at work in him."
for Herod had earlier seized John and bound him in fetters and put him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother.
For John had been saying to him: "It is not lawful for you to have her as your wife."
And although he wanted to kill him, he feared the people, because they held him to be a prophet.
And when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in their midst, and her dancing pleased Herod.
Because of this he promised her with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
And she, having been prompted beforehand by her mother, said: "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
And although the king was grieved, on account of the oath and those reclining at table with him he commanded that it be given to her.
And he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
And they brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took away his body and buried it, and they came and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there by boat and went to a deserted place by himself. And when the people heard of it, they followed him on foot from the cities.
And Jesus came out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.

And when evening came, his disciples came to him and said to him: "This place is deserted, and the hour is already past; send this crowd away, so that they may go into the surrounding villages and buy food for themselves."
But Jesus said to them: "They need not go away; you give them something to eat."
And they said to him: "We have nothing here but five loaves and two fish."
Jesus said to them: "Bring them here to me!"

And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the grass. And he took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven and blessed, and broke, and gave the bread to his disciples, and the disciples gave it to the crowd.
All ate and were filled; and they took up the leftover fragments, twelve baskets full.
And those who ate were five thousand men alone, apart from children and women.
And immediately he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he dismissed the crowd.
And when he had dismissed the crowd, he went up the mountain by himself to pray. And when evening came, he was there alone.
But the boat was many stadia away from land and was battered by the waves, for the wind was against it.
And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified and said: "It is some apparition," and they cried out from fear.
Immediately Jesus spoke to them and said to them, "Take courage! It is I; do not be afraid!"
Peter answered and said to him, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on these waters."
And he said, "Come!" And Peter got down out of the boat and walked on the waters, and was coming toward Jesus.
And when he saw the strong wind, he became afraid and began to sink, and he cried out and said: "Lord, save me!"
And immediately he stretched out his hand, took hold of him and said to him: "O you of little faith, why did you doubt?"
And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind ceased.
And those who were in the boat came to him and worshiped him and said to him: Truly you are the Son of God.
And they went out and came to the land of Gennesaret.
And the men of that place recognized him and sent word into all that surrounding region, and brought to him all who were badly afflicted.
And they begged him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment. And as many as touched it were healed.
Then Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus and said:
"Why do your disciples break the teaching of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
But Jesus answered and said to them, "And why do you also break the commandment of God by your teaching?
For God said: Honor your father and your mother; and whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him die.
But you say: Whoever says to his father or his mother: The gift by which you would have had benefit from me [is an offering],
and does not honor his father or his mother—by such things you make the word of God void through your teaching.
Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied rightly about you, saying:
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far removed from me;
in vain they serve me, for they teach the teaching and commandment of men.
And he called the crowd to him and said to them: Listen and understand:
It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth, that defiles a person.
Then his disciples came to Jesus and said to him: Do you know that when the Pharisees heard that saying, they took offense?
But he answered and said to them: Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted.
Leave them; they are blind and leaders of the blind. For if a blind person leads a blind person, they go astray and both fall into a pit.
Peter answered and said to him: Explain this parable to us.
But Jesus said to him: Are you also still without understanding?
Do you not know that everything that goes in through the mouth goes into the belly and goes out through the outlet?
But what comes out of the mouth comes out of the heart, and that defiles a person.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false accusations, blasphemies.
These are what defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person."
And Jesus went away from there and came to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders, crying out and saying: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David, for my daughter is grievously possessed by a demon.
But Jesus did not answer her a word. And the disciples came to Jesus and said to him: "Send her away, for she is crying out after us."
Jesus said to them: "I have not been sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
But she came and worshiped him and said to him: Lord, have mercy on me!
But he answered and said to her: It is not good to take bread from the children and to put it before the dogs.
And she said: "Yes, Lord, for even the dogs eat of the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
Then Jesus answered and said to her: "O woman! Great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed from that hour.
And Jesus went away from there and came to the shore of the Sea of Galilee, and he went up on the mountain and sat down there.

And a great crowd came to him, who had with them the lame, the blind, the deaf, those who crawl along the ground, and many others seized by diseases of various kinds. And they set them at his feet, and he healed them.
And indeed the crowd marveled when they saw how the deaf spoke, and the lame walked, and the crooked were healed, and the blind saw, and they glorified the God of Israel.

But Jesus called his disciples and said: I have pity on this crowd, for behold, it is now three days that they have been waiting for me, and they have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away fasting, lest they collapse on the road.
His disciples said to him: Where would we get so much bread in the wilderness, to satisfy so great a crowd?
Jesus said to them: How much bread do you have here? And they said to him: Seven loaves and a few fish.
And he ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground.
And he took those seven loaves and the fish and gave thanks and broke them and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
They all ate and were filled; and they took up what was left of the broken pieces, seven baskets full.
And those who ate were four thousand men, not counting children and women.
And he dismissed the crowd, and Jesus went up into the boat and came to the borders of Magdala.
And the Pharisees and Sadducees came to him, testing him, so that he would show them a sign from heaven.
But he answered and said to them: "When evening comes, you say, 'It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.'
And at dawn you say: There will be stormy weather, for the sky is red [?] and gloomy. Hypocrites, you know how to discern the face of the sky, but you cannot understand the signs of the times.
An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. And he left them and went away.
And his disciples came from the other side, and they had forgotten to take bread.
And Jesus said to them: "Watch out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
And they reasoned among themselves, saying: "We did not bring any bread."
Jesus perceived it and said to them: Why are you reasoning in your hearts, you of little faith, because you have no bread?
Do you not yet understand, and do you not remember the five loaves and the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
Nor the seven loaves and the four thousand, and how many large baskets you took up?
How is it that you do not understand that it was not about bread that I said to you: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which is hypocrisy?
Then they understood that he had not told them to beware of leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, he questioned his disciples and said: What do people say about me? That the Son of Man is who?
And they said: "Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
And he said to them: Who do you think I am?
Simon Peter answered and said to him: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Jesus answered and said to him: Blessed are you, Simon bar Jonah, for flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my heavenly Father.
And I say to you: You are the rock, and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not overcome it.
And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
Then he commanded his disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.

From that time Jesus began to make known to his disciples that he must go up to Jerusalem and suffer greatly from the chief priests and scribes and elders of the people, and be killed, and rise on the third day.
And Peter came to him and began to rebuke him, and said to him: "Mercy on you, Lord; may it not be so."
But he turned to Peter and said to him: "Get away from me, Satan; you are a stumbling block to me, for you are not thinking the things of God, but the things of men."
Then Jesus said to his disciples: Whoever wishes to follow me and come, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
If anyone wishes to save his own self, he will lose it; and whoever loses his own self for my sake will find it.
What profit will it be to a person if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul? Or what will a person give in exchange for his soul?
For the Son of Man is to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each person according to their deeds.
Amen I say to you: There are some of those standing here who will not see the taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.
And after six days Jesus took Peter and James and John his brother, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
And he was changed before them into another appearance, and his face shone like the sun, and his garment was white as snow.
And Moses and Elijah appeared to them with him, and they were conversing with him.
Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here. Do you wish us to make three tents here: one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah?
And while he was still saying this, behold, a cloud of light overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud and said: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him!
When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid.
Jesus came, touched them with his hand, and said to them: Get up, do not be afraid!
And they raised their eyes and saw no one except Jesus alone.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: Tell no one about this vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
And the disciples questioned him, saying to him: Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
But Jesus answered and said to them: Elijah will come and will restore all things.
But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. And in the same way the Son of Man must suffer at their hands.
Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
And when they came to the crowd, a man came to him and knelt before him, saying to him:
Lord, have mercy on my son, for from time to time [?] he is severely tormented, for he often falls into the fire and often into the water.
And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not heal him.
Jesus answered and said to him: O unbelieving and perverse generation! How long am I to be with you, how long am I to bear with you? Bring him here to me!
And when they brought him, Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out of him. And the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus by themselves and said to him: Why could we not drive it out?

And he said to them: Because of your little faith. Amen, I say to you: if you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, Move from here to there! And it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.
But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.
And as they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: The Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of men,
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise." And they were greatly distressed.
And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma came to him and said to Peter: Does your teacher not pay the didrachma?

And he said: Yes. And when they went into the house, Jesus spoke to him first and said to Peter: What do you think, Simon: from whom do the kings of the earth take tribute or toll, from their sons or from strangers?
Peter said to him: From strangers. Jesus answered and said to him: Then the sons are indeed free.

But so that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, open its mouth, and you will find in it a stater. Take that and give it to them for you and for me.
Then the disciples came to Jesus and said to him: Who then will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
And Jesus called the children and set them in their midst
and said: "Amen, I tell you: unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
For whoever humbles himself like this child, he will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever receives one such child in my name receives me.

And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey-driven millstone were hung around his neck and he were drowned in the depths of the sea.
Woe to this world because of stumbling blocks, for the stumbling block is bound to come, even unwillingly; but woe to that man through whom the stumbling block comes.

If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life lame or without a hand than to have two hands and two feet and fall into that eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter life one-eyed than to have two eyes and enter the Gehenna of fire.
Take care that you do not despise any one of these little ones. I tell you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of my Father who is in the heavens.
Now the Son of Man also has come to seek, that he may save the lost sheep.
What do you think: if some man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave those ninety-nine on the mountains and go and seek the one that went astray?
And when he finds it, amen I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that had not gone astray.
So it is the will of my heavenly Father that not one of these little ones should perish.
If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him when you and he are alone. If he listens to you, you will have gained your brother;
if he does not listen to you, take with you one or two others, so that by the mouth of two and three witnesses every word may be established.
If he does not listen to them either, tell the congregation; and if he does not listen to the congregation either, let him be to you as a tribute collector and a publican.
Amen I say to you: whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in the heavens.
Again I say to you: if two of you agree on earth about any matter whatever that they ask for, it shall be done for them by my heavenly Father.
For wherever two or three are gathered for the sake of my name, there I am among them.
Then Peter came up to Jesus and said to him: Lord, how many times may my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?
Jesus said to him: I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
And when he began to settle them, they brought before him one who owed ten thousand talents.
And since he had nothing to give, his lord commanded that he be sold, with his wife and his children and whatever he had, and that payment be made.
That servant fell down, bowed in worship before him and said to him: Be patient with me, and I will give you everything.
The lord had pity on that servant and released him, and also forgave him the debt.
And as that servant went out from there, he found one of his fellows who owed him a hundred drachmas; he seized him and was choking him, saying to him: Give me what you owe.
His fellow fell down before him, begged him and said to him: Be patient with me, and I will give it to you.
But he did not listen to him; rather, he afflicted him all the more and threw him into prison until he should pay him the debt.
When his fellows saw this thing, they were greatly distressed, and they went and informed their lord of everything that had happened.
Then his lord summoned him and said to him: Wicked servant, I forgave you all your debt because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?"
And his lord became angry with him and handed him over to the torturers until he should pay off all that debt.
So too will your heavenly Father do to you, if each of you does not forgive his fellow with all your heart.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came to the borders of Judea, beyond the Jordan.
And a great multitude followed him, and he healed them there.
Then the Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying to him: Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for any fault?
But Jesus answered and said to them: "Have you not read that he who created them in the beginning made them male and female?"
And he said: 'For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh.'
that they are no longer two, but one flesh. Those whom God has joined together, let men not separate.
But they said to him: "Why then did Moses command that a certificate of divorce be given, and that she be sent away?"
Jesus answered and said to them: Because of your hardness of heart Moses commanded you to put away your wives, but in the beginning it was not so.
But I say to you that whoever puts away his wife, except for fornication, and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries a woman who has been put away also commits adultery.
His disciples said to him: If the fault of a man with regard to a woman is so great, it is not fitting to marry.
Jesus said to them: "Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were born eunuchs from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever is able to accept it, let him accept it."
Then children were brought to him, so that he might lay his hand on them and bless them. But the disciples were angry with them.
But Jesus said to them: Let those children come to me, and do not hinder them at all, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.
And he laid his hand on them. And as he went away from there,
behold, a certain man came to him and said: Good teacher, what good thing should I do, so that I may have eternal life?
But Jesus said to him: Why do you ask me about a good deed? One is good: God. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.
He said to him: Which commandments? And Jesus said to him: These: You shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness,
honor your father and your mother, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
The young man said to him: All these I have kept from my childhood. What do I still lack?
Jesus said to him: If you wish to be perfect, go and sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
And when the young man heard this, he went away sorrowful, for he was very rich.
But Jesus said to his disciples: "Amen, I say to you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.
And again I say to you: it is easier for the rope of a winch to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
When his disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and said: Who then is able to be saved?
Jesus looked at them and said to them: For men it is impossible, but with God everything is possible.
Then Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will there be for us?

But Jesus said to them: Amen I say to you that you who have followed me, at that future coming, when the Son of Man sits on the thrones of his glory, you also shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who leaves house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land for the sake of my name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a man, the master of a house, who went out at dawn to hire laborers for his vineyard,
and he promised them a wage of a drachma each per day and sent them into his vineyard.
And he went out at the third hour and saw others standing idle in the streets,
and he said to them: You also go to my vineyard, and whatever is just I will give you.
And they went. And then he went out at the sixth and the ninth hour and did the same.
And at the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and he said to them: Why do you stand here idle all day?
But they said to him: No one has hired us. He said to them: You also go to my vineyard.
And when evening came, the lord of the house said to his steward: Call the laborers and give them their wages; begin with the last and go on to the first.
Those of the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
Those of the first hour came too, and they thought that they would receive more; and they too each received a denarius.
And when they had received it, they grumbled against the householder,
And they said: These last ones worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the heat.
But he answered one of them and said: Friend, I do you no wrong. Did I not promise you one drachma?
Take what is yours and go. But I wish to give to this last one just as to you.
Or is it not right for me to do what I wish with what is mine? But perhaps your eye is evil, while I am good.
So the last will be first and the first last, for many are called and few are chosen.
And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them:
Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death.
And they will hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and tortured and crucified, and on the third day he will rise.
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to Jesus with her sons, worshiping him and asking something of him.
And he said to her: What do you wish? She said to him: Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.

Jesus answered and said to them: You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am to drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized? And they said to him: We are able.

Jesus said to them: My cup you will indeed drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized, but to sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to give; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.
When the ten heard this, they became angry with the two brothers.
But Jesus called them and said: Do you know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them?
But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be great among you, let him be your servant;
and whoever among you wishes to be first, let him be your slave.
Just as the Son of Man did not come so that anyone should serve him, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.
And as they were going out of Jericho, a great crowd followed him.
And behold, two blind men were sitting by the road. And when they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out with a loud voice: Have mercy on us, Jesus, Son of David!
But the crowd rebuked them, so that they would be silent. But they cried out all the more: Have mercy on us, Lord Jesus, Son of David!
Jesus stopped and called them and said: What do you wish that I should do for you?
They said to him: "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes, and immediately they received their sight and followed him.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and to Bethany, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two of his disciples
and said to them: "Go into the village that is in front of you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me."
