And if anyone says anything to you, say: The Lord has need of them, and immediately he will send them.
All this took place so that the word of the prophet might be fulfilled, which said:
Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, gentle, and he sits on a donkey and a colt, the offspring of a beast of burden.
And the disciples went and did just as Jesus had commanded them.
And they brought the donkey and the colt with it, and they laid garments on it, and he sat on it.
And the greater part of the crowd spread their garments on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

And the people who went ahead and those who followed behind were crying out and saying: Blessed is the King, the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, blessed is the King who is in the highest!
And when he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and said: "Who is this?"
But the people said: This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
And Jesus entered the temple and drove out all the sellers and all who were buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and upset the seats of those who sold doves.
And he said to them: "It is written: 'My house shall be called a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
And when the chief priests and the scribes saw the miracles that Jesus had done, and the children who were crying out in the temple and saying: Hosanna to the Son of David,
they became angry and said to him: Do you hear what these are saying? But Jesus said to them: Yes; have you never read: From the mouth of nursing infants praise has been established?
And he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and he stayed there.
And the next day, as he was coming to the city, he became hungry.
And he saw a fig tree by the road and came to it, and he found nothing on it but leaves only. And he said to it: Let there be no more fruit from you forever! And the fig tree withered at once.
When the disciples saw it, they were amazed and said: How quickly this fig tree has withered!

Jesus answered and said to them, "Amen, I say to you: if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to this fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be uprooted from here and fall into the sea!', it will be so.
And everything that you ask for in prayer with faith, it will be done for you.

And when he came to the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached him as he was teaching the people, and they said to him: By what authority do you do this, and who gave you this authority?
Jesus answered and said to them: I too will ask you one question; if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do this.
The baptism of John, where was it from: from heaven or from men? And they reasoned among themselves and said: If we say, From heaven, he will say to us: Why then did you not believe him?
If we say, From men, we are afraid of this people, for all hold John to be a prophet.
And they answered Jesus and said: We do not know. He in turn said to them: Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this.
Now what do you think? A certain man had two sons. He came to the first and said, 'Son, go today and work in my vineyard.'
And he answered and said: I will go, lord; and he did not go.
And he came to the second and said the same. But he answered and said: I do not want to, I will not go. But afterward he repented and went.

Which of these two did the will of his father? They said to him: The latter. Jesus said to them: Amen I say to you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and sinners believed him; and you saw it and did not repent afterward, so as to believe him.

Hear another parable: There was a man, a master of a household, who planted a vineyard and put a wall around it and made a winepress in it and built a tower, and he gave it to tenants to work and went away.
And when the time of the fruit arrived, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive his fruit.
And the tenants seized his servants; some they beat, some they killed, and some they stoned.
Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they did the same to them too.
And last of all he sent his son to them and said: Perhaps they will respect my son?
But when those tenant farmers saw his son, they said in their hearts: This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and seize his inheritance.
And they seized him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
So when the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenant farmers?
They said to him: He will destroy those evil men in an evil way and give the vineyard to other tenant farmers, who will give him the fruit in its season.
Jesus said to them: Have you not read in the scriptures: The stone that the builders despised has become the head of the corner? This was from the Lord, and it is wonderful before our eyes.
Therefore I say to you: The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
And whoever falls on that stone will be shattered, and on whomever it falls, it will scatter him to nothing.
And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard this parable of his, they understood that he had spoken about them,
and they sought to seize him, but they were afraid of the people, for they held him to be a prophet.
And again Jesus answered them in a parable and said:
The kingdom of God is like a man, a king, who made a wedding feast for his son
and he sent out his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, but they did not want to come.

Again he sent other servants and said: Tell those who have been invited: Behold, I have prepared my meal; my young bulls and my fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to this wedding feast.
But they paid no attention and went away, one to his own farm and another to his business.
And others seized his servants, insulted them, and killed them.
But the king became angry and sent his troops, and he destroyed those murderers and burned their city with fire.
Then he said to his servants: 'The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
Go out to where the roads go out of the city, and invite to the wedding feast as many as you find.'
And his servants went out onto the roads and gathered everyone they found, both bad and good, and the wedding feast was filled with guests.
And when the king came in to see the guests at table, he saw there a man who was not wearing a wedding garment.
And he said to him: Friend, how did you come in here without wearing a wedding garment? But he was silent.
Then the king said to his attendants: 'Bind his hands and feet and throw him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.'
For many are invited, but few are chosen.
Then the Pharisees went away and took counsel concerning him, how they might trap him in his speech.

And they sent their disciples to him together with the Herodians, and they said: Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God truthfully, and you are not concerned about anyone, for you do not regard a person's face.
Now tell us, what do you think: is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?
Jesus perceived their wickedness and said to them, "Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
Show me the coin of the tribute!" And they brought him a denarius.
Jesus said to them, "Whose is this image and inscription?"
They said to him, "Caesar's." Then Jesus said to them, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
And when they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
On that day the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him and asked him,
saying, "Teacher, Moses said this: If anyone dies and has no child, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
There were among us seven brothers. The first married and died, and no offspring remained, and he left his wife to his brother.
Likewise the second and the third, up to the seventh.
Last of all, the woman also died.
Now then, in the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her."
Jesus answered and said to them, "You are mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in heaven.
And concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken by God, who says:
'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob'? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
And when the crowd heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.
But when the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
And one of them asked him, testing him:
"Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?"
And Jesus said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbour as yourself.
On these two commandments hang all the Law and the Prophets."
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them,
And he said: What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he? And they said to him: David's.
Jesus said to them: How then does David, by the Spirit, call him Lord, saying:
The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet?
If David calls him Lord, how is he his son?
And no one could answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to question him any more.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowd and to his disciples,
And he said: The scribes and the Pharisees have sat down on the seats of Moses,
Everything that they tell you, keep and do, but do not act according to their deeds, for they say and do not do.
For they bind heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger.
And they do all their deeds to be seen by people: they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the fringes of their garments.
they love the place of honor at supper and the first seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called by people: "Rabbi! Rabbi!"
But as for you, call no one rabbi, for one is your teacher, Christ, and you are all brothers.
And call no one on earth your father, for one is your Father, who is in heaven.
Nor let yourselves be called leaders, for one is your leader, Christ.
But the greatest among you shall be your servant.
And whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who devour the houses of widows and for a pretext pray at length. Therefore you will receive the greater judgment.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you shut the kingdom of heaven before people; you do not enter, and you do not allow those who are entering to enter.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you travel about over sea and dry land to make a single proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him a child of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides, who say: "Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound by his oath."
Fools and blind! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?
And you say: 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the offering that is on the altar is bound.'
Fools and blind! Which is greater: the offering, or the altar that sanctifies the offering?
But whoever has sworn by the altar swears by it and by everything that is on it.
And whoever has sworn by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it.
And whoever has sworn by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you take the tithe of mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith. These you ought to do, and not to neglect those.
Blind leaders, who strain out the gnat and swallow the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but the inside is full of plunder and impurity.
Blind Pharisees, first cleanse the inside of the cup, so that the outside too may be clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful before people, but inside are full of the bones of the dead and of all impurity.
So you too outwardly seem righteous to people, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the memorials of the righteous.
And you say: 'If we had been alive in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.'
Thus by this you testify against yourselves that you are the children of those who murdered the prophets.
And now you, too, fill up the measure of your fathers.
You serpents and offspring of vipers, how will you ever escape the judgment of Gehenna?
Therefore, behold, I am sending you prophets, wise men and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will torment in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
So that all the righteous blood shed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
Amen I say to you: all this will come upon this generation.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who slaughtered the prophets and stoned those sent to you, how many times I wanted to gather your children, as a bird gathers its chicks under its wings, and you were not willing!
Behold, your houses are left to you desolate.
But I say to you: you will not see me again from now on, until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
And Jesus came out of the temple and was going away. And his disciples came up to him and were showing him the building of the temple.
But Jesus answered and said to them: Do you indeed see all this? Amen I say to you: not a stone will remain upon a stone, until all of it is torn down.
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately and said, "Tell us, when will this be, and what is the sign of your coming and of the end of this world?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "Take care that no one leads you astray,
For many will come in my name and will say: I am the Christ, and they will lead many astray.
And you will hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for this must happen, but it is not yet the end.
Nation will rise up against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in place after place,
for all this is the beginning of the birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.
And then many will stumble, and they will hand one another over and hate one another.
And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
And because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
When you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place, let the one who reads understand.
Then let whoever is in Judea flee to the mountain.
And let whoever is on the roof not come down to take anything from his house.
And let whoever is out in the field not turn back again to take his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days!
But pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the Sabbath day.
For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will be.
And if those days were not shortened, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you: Look, here is the Christ, or: There, do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform very great miracles and signs, so as to lead astray, if somehow they could, even the elect.
Behold, I have told you beforehand.
If they say to you: He is in the desert, do not go out; Look, he is in the inner chambers, do not believe it.
For as the lightning flashes out from the east and is seen as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will gather.
But immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the heavens, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, beating their breasts, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the edge of heaven to its other edge.
But learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and the leaf comes out, know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of heaven nor the Son, but the Father alone.
As it was in the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For as they were in those days before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day when Noah entered the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and swept everything away, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two will be out in the field: one will be taken, and one will be left.
Two women will be grinding flour: one will be taken, and one will be left.
Keep watch, then, for you do not know on what day your Lord will come.
But know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was going to come, he would have kept watch and would not have let the wall of his house be dug through.
Therefore you also must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.
Who, then, is that faithful and wise servant, whom his lord will set over his attendants to give them their food at its proper time?
Blessed is that servant whose lord comes and finds him doing so.
Amen, I say to you that he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My lord is delaying his coming,'
and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with drunkards,
the lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour that he does not know.
And he will cut him in two and assign him his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took up their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
The foolish ones took their lamps and did not take oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil with them in their vessels along with their lamps.
And as the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
Right at midnight there was a cry: 'Behold, the bridegroom is coming! Rise, and let us go out to meet him.'
Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.
The foolish said to the wise, "Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out."
The wise ones answered and said to them, 'Perhaps there will not be enough for us and for you; instead, go to the market and buy for yourselves.'
And as they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with the bridegroom to the wedding, and the door was shut.
Afterward the other virgins also came and said, 'Lord, lord, open to us too!'
He answered and said to them, 'Amen, I say to you, I do not know you.'
Keep watch, then, you also, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
It is as when a man is setting out on a journey, and he gives instructions to his servants and hands over his property to them.
To one he gave five talents, that is, kankars, to another two kankars, and to another one, to each according to his ability, and he went away.
And immediately the one who had received the five talents went and worked with them, and he gained another five.
In the same way, the one who had received two gained another two.
But the one who had received one went, dug in the ground, and buried his lord's silver.
After a long time the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with those servants.
And the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought him another five talents and said to him: Lord, you gave me five talents; behold, I have gained another five talents.
His lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord!
The one who had received the two talents came and said to him: Lord, you gave me two talents; behold, I have gained another two.
His lord said to him: Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord!
The one who had received one talent also came and said to him: Lord, know that you are a hard man: you reap where you did not sow and you gather where you did not scatter.
I was afraid, and I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Here, behold, you have what is yours.
His lord answered and said to him: Wicked and obstinate servant! Know that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter.
You ought to have placed my silver at the place of trade, and I would have come and received what is mine with interest.
Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
For to everyone who has, it will be given and added; and from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
"And cast that useless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all his angels with him, then he will sit on the thrones of his glory.
And all the nations will gather before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
And he will set the sheep at his right and the goats at the left.
Then the King will say to those at his right hand: "Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you welcomed me;
I was naked, and you clothed me; I was sick, and you looked after me; I was in prison, and you came to me.
Then the righteous will answer him and say: "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you? Or thirsty and give you drink?
When did we see you a stranger and welcome you? Or naked and clothe you?
When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?"
And the King will answer and say to them: Amen, I say to you: inasmuch as you did it to one of these least of my brothers, you did it to me.
Then he will say to those at the left: Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his servants,
for I was hungry, and you did not give me food; I was thirsty, and you did not give me drink;
I was a stranger, and you did not take me in; I was naked, and you did not clothe me; I was sick and in prison, and you did not come to me."
Then they too will answer and say to him: Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, or in a foreign land, or in nakedness, or in weakness, or in prison, and did not serve you?
Then he will answer and say to them: Amen, I say to you: inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least, you did not do it to me.
And these will go away into eternal torment, but the righteous into eternal life.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples:
Do you know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified?
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the court of Caiaphas the high priest.
And they took counsel to seize Jesus by treachery.
But they said: Not during this feast, so that there may be no uproar among the people.
Now while Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
A woman came to him who had an alabaster flask of very costly ointment, and she poured it on his head as he reclined at table.
When the disciples saw it, they grew angry and said: Why was this ointment wasted?
This could have been sold for a great sum and given to the poor.
Jesus understood and said to them: Why do you trouble that woman? For she has done a good deed toward me.
For the poor are always with you, but I am not always with you.
For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.
Amen, I say to you: wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.
Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said: "What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?" And they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
And from then on he sought a suitable time to hand him over to them.
Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples of Jesus came and said to him: Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat this Passover?
And Jesus said to them: Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: The Teacher says this: My time is near; I will keep this Passover at your house with my disciples.
And the disciples did as Jesus had commanded them.
And when evening came, Jesus reclined at table with the twelve.
And as they were eating, Jesus said: "Amen, I tell you: one of you will betray me."
And they were greatly distressed, and each one of them began to say: Surely it is not I, Lord?
But he answered and said to them: "The one who dips his hand with me in this dish, he will betray me."
The Son of Man indeed goes, as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed. It would have been better for him if that man had not been born.
Judas, who betrayed him, answered and said: Surely it is not I, Teacher? Jesus said to him: You have said it.
And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it and broke it, and gave it to his disciples and said to them: Take, eat; this is my body.
And he took a cup and gave thanks, gave it to them and said: Drink from this, all of you.
this is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
But I say to you: from now on I will no longer drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.
And they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them: All of you will stumble because of me this night, for it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of his flock will be scattered.
But after my rising I will go before you into Galilee."
Peter answered and said: Even if all the others stumble because of you, I will never stumble because of you.
Jesus said to him: "Amen, I tell you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."
Peter said to him: Even if it means my death with you, I will never deny you. And all the disciples said likewise.
Then Jesus came with them to a village called Gethsemane, and he said to them: Sit here until I go over there and pray.
And he took along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and he began to be sorrowful and anguished.
Then Jesus said to them: "My soul is distressed even to death; stay here and keep watch with me."
And he went on a little farther and fell on his face, praying and saying: Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as you will.
And he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter: Were you not able even for one hour to keep watch with me?
Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation; the spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
Again, a second time, Jesus went away and prayed and said: My Father, if it is not possible for this cup to pass by me without my drinking it, let your will be done.
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And he left them and went away again a third time and prayed, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them: Sleep from now on and rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go from here. Behold, my betrayer has arrived.
And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the elders of the people.
Now his betrayer had given an instruction, saying: The one I kiss, he is the one; seize him.
And at once he came up to Jesus and said to him: "Rejoice, Teacher!" And he kissed him.
But Jesus said to him: Friend, is it for this that you have come? Then they came up and laid their hands on Jesus and seized him.
And one of those with Jesus reached out his hand and drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him: Return the sword to its place! For all who take up the sword will perish by the sword.
Or do you think that I cannot ask my Father, and he would now set beside me here more than twelve legions of angels?
And how then would those Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must be so?
At that time Jesus said to the crowd: You have come out as against a robber, with sword and clubs, to seize me. Day after day I sat with you in the temple and taught you, and you did not seize me.
All this happened so that the books of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him and fled.
But they seized Jesus and took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders of the people had gathered.
But Peter followed him from a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and he went inside and sat with the attendants to see the outcome.
But the high priests and the whole assembly were seeking false witnesses against Jesus so that they might kill him,
and they did not find any, though many false witnesses had come. At last two came forward
and said: This man said this: I am able to destroy this temple of God and on the third day to build it.
Then the high priest stood up and said to him: Do you answer nothing at all to what these men testify against you?
But Jesus was silent. Then the high priest said to him: I adjure you by the living God to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus said to him: You have said it. But I say to you: from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the powers and coming with the clouds of heaven.
Then the high priest tore his garment and said: What further need do we have of witnesses? Behold, you have heard his blasphemy.
What is your wish?" And they answered and said to him: "He deserves death."
Then they spat in his face and struck him on the head with their fists, and some slapped him on the cheek.
and said to him: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?"
But Peter was sitting in the courtyard. And a servant girl came up to him and said to him: You too were with Jesus the Galilean.
But he denied it before everyone and said: I do not know what you are saying.
And as he went out outside the gate, another girl saw him and said to those standing there: This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.
And again Peter denied it with an oath and said, "I do not know the man."
And after a little while those who were standing there came up to Peter and said to him: "Truly you also are one of them, for your speech also gives you away."
Then Peter began to curse and to swear: "I do not know that man." And immediately a cock crowed.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said to him: "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times." And Peter went outside and wept bitterly.
And when day dawned, the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel concerning Jesus, in order to put him to death.
And they bound him and led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Then when Judas, who had handed him over, saw that he had been condemned, he repented and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders
and said: "I have sinned, for I have handed over righteous blood." But they said to him: "What is that to us? You know!"
And he scattered the silver in the temple and departed and went away from there and hanged himself and died.
But the chief priests took the silver and said: "It is not lawful to put this in the holy place, because it is the price of blood."
And they took counsel and took the silver and with it bought the potter's field as a burial place for strangers.
For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, who says: "And I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was sold, whom the sons of Israel bought,"
and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord commanded me."
But Jesus stood before the governor. And the governor questioned him and said to him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him: "You say so."
And to the accusation of the chief priests and the elders he answered nothing.
Then Pilate said to him, "Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?"
And he gave him no answer, not to a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
Now at the festivals the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whomever they wished.
And there was at that time a certain notorious prisoner who was called Jesus Barabbas.
And when they had gathered, Pilate said to them: "Which of these two do you want me to release to you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
And as Pilate sat on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him and said: "What is there between you and that righteous man? For I have suffered much in a vision today because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus.
The governor answered and said to them: "Which of these two do you want me to release to you?" And they said: "Barabbas."
Pilate said to them: "Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?" They all said to him: "Let him be crucified!"
But he said to them: "And what evil has he done?" But they cried out all the more, saying: "Let him be crucified!"

When Pilate saw that it was doing him no good, but rather that a tumult was arising, he asked for water and washed his hands before the people and said: "I am innocent of the blood of this man; see to it yourselves."
And all the people answered and said: "His blood be on us and on our children."
Then he released Barabbas to them, but he had Jesus scourged with a whip and handed him over to them to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole company around him.
And they stripped him and put a purple cloak on him.
And they wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand, and knelt before him and mocked him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!"
And they spat on him, and took the reed and struck him on the head.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped the cloak off him and clothed him in his own garments and led him away to crucify him.
And as they went out from there, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon. They pressed him into forced service to carry his cross.
And they came to the place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull.
They gave him vinegar mixed with gall, and when he had received it, he would not drink.

And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments and cast lots, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled, which says: They divided my garments among them, and over my tunic they cast lots.
And they sat and guarded him there.
And they placed over his head the charge against him, written: This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.
Then they crucified with him two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.
And those who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads
And they were saying: Aha, you who would destroy the temple and build it up on the third day, save yourself now! If you are the Son of God, come down from that cross!
Likewise the chief priests, together with the scribes and the elders, were mocking and saying:
He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down now from that cross, and we will believe him.
If he trusted in God, let God save him, if he desires him, for he said: I am the Son of God.
Likewise the robbers who were crucified with him reproached him.
But from the sixth hour darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
And at about the ninth hour Jesus called out with a loud voice and said: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? That is: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
And some of those standing there heard this and said: This man is calling Elijah.
And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled it with vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink.
But the others said: Leave him be, and let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.
But Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and gave up the spirit.
And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook, and the rocks split
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
and they came out of their tombs after his resurrection and entered the holy city and appeared to many.
But the centurion and those with him, who were guarding Jesus, saw the earthquake and what had happened, and they were greatly afraid and said: Truly this was the Son of God.
And many women were also there, watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him,
among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
And when evening came, a rich man from Arimathea came, named Joseph, who had also been a disciple of Jesus.
This man came to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered his body to be given.
And Joseph took his body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
and laid it in his new tomb, which he had hewn out of the rock, and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene was there and another Mary, and they were sitting before the tomb.
On the next day, which is after Friday, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
and said to him, "Lord, we have remembered that that deceiver said while he was still alive, 'After three days I will rise.'

Now command that the tomb be secured until the third day, lest his disciples come and steal him away and tell the people that he has risen from the dead. And the last deception will be worse than the first.
Pilate said to them: You have a guard; go and secure it as you know how.
And they came and secured the tomb and sealed the stone, together with the guard.
On the evening of the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, came and rolled the stone away from the door of the tomb and sat upon it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
Out of fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.
The angel answered and said to the women: Do not be afraid; I know that you are seeking Jesus of Nazareth, the crucified one.
He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where they laid him.
And go quickly and tell his disciples: He has risen, and behold, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. There you will see him. Behold, I have told you.
And they went away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy; they ran to tell his disciples.
And behold, Jesus met them and said: Rejoice! And they came up to him and fell at his feet and worshiped him.
Then Jesus said to them: Do not be afraid! Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.
And as these women went, behold, some of the guard entered the city and told the chief priests all that had happened.
They gathered with the elders and took counsel, and they gave a large sum of silver to the soldiers
And they said: Say this, that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep.
If the governor hears of this, we will persuade him and keep you free of trouble."
They took the silver and did as they had been taught by them. And this story has been spread among the Jews to this very day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
And they saw him and worshiped him, but some doubted.
Jesus came up to them, spoke to them and said: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. As the Father sent me, I also send you.
Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
And teach them to keep everything that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you all the days, even to the end of the world.
